$comment: Hand-compiled from the vendors' official advisory pages (see sources and read_at); facts only, no advisory text. Every rule is a preliminary suggestion until the responsible team confirms it. See docs/notes/c2-firmware-advisory.md (Rule table).

rules.title: Return Address Security Bulletin

match.note: Desktop table, Ryzen 5000 columns (Vermeer, Cezanne): minimum AGESA ComboAM4v2PI 1.2.0.B, dated 2023-08-25 in the table; the table gives the minimum version to update to
Desktop table, Ryzen 7000 column: minimum AGESA 1.0.8.0, dated 2023-08-25 in the table; the table names the family ComboAM5, the image string uses ComboAM5PI

review.preliminary_by: 韌體分析（C2 角色）初審

rules.note: Zen 3 and Zen 4 client parts only; the bulletin also offers a standalone microcode patch as an alternative to the AGESA update, which this rule does not evaluate

rules.title: SMM Lock Bypass

match.note: Client desktop table: Ryzen 3000 (Matisse) lists ComboAM4v2PI 1.2.0Cc (2024-08-16); Ryzen 5000 (Vermeer, Cezanne) and Ryzen 4000 (Renoir) list 1.2.0.cb (2024-07-30); fixed_in is the highest of them, so an image at 1.2.0.Cb is still reported as affected
Client desktop table: Ryzen 7000 (Raphael) lists ComboAM5PI 1.2.0.1 (2024-08-07)

Data Center table, mitigation option 2 (hot-loadable microcode), Naples row; the page names CPUID 0x00800F12; equivalence id 0x8012 is CPUID 00800F12 in the equivalence table of the public linux-firmware AMD microcode container (fam17h)

review.preliminary_by: 韌體分析（C2 角色）初審

rules.note: AGESA conditions: client platforms only (the bulletin's embedded tables are not in this rule); the bulletin lists the fix per CPU, the image does not say which CPU it is for. Microcode conditions: only the data center rows, which name a CPUID and a patch level; the client tables list no microcode level and are not machine-comparable. The microcode conditions are keyed by equivalence id, so they also hit a client-board image that carries the same equivalence id; the bulletin presents the microcode as an alternative to the PI update

rules.note: Only the data center microcode levels (EPYC 7001, 7002, 7003, 9004, 9005), each tied to a CPUID in the page's CPUID table. The client, workstation, mobile and embedded tables list platform initialization versions only, no microcode level, so they are not machine-comparable and not in this rule. The conditions are keyed by equivalence id, so they also hit a client-board image that carries the same equivalence id (for example Naples B2, CPUID 00800F12); the page lists the level as the minimum version, with PI releases as the way to deliver it

match.note: 14.0 line: the bulletin lists CSME and AMT builds below 14.0.45 as affected
14.5 line: the bulletin lists CSME and AMT builds below 14.5.25 as affected

review.preliminary_by: 韌體分析（C2 角色）初審

rules.note: Only the 14.x thresholds of the bulletin's CSME version list are in this rule. The 14.0.45 and 14.5.25 thresholds match the NVD CPE version ranges of the CVEs that NVD links to this advisory; CVE-2020-27336, CVE-2020-27337 and CVE-2020-27338 have no NVD record with an Intel CPE or a reference to this advisory (not checked). The bulletin's version list gives 11.8.82 for the 11.8 line (some CVE descriptions on the same page and the NVD CPE ranges say 11.8.80); this rule does not use the 11.x lines
